newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says not out to keep power at any cost.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says not out to keep power at any cost.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Tuesday said he was not negotiating with New Zealand First to be in government at any cost.

It is not a negotiation at any cost, it's seeking to advance the general programme that we have put in place, but acknowledging that all coalitions will require consultation, compromise and common sense," Bolger said.
After the general election on Saturday, nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power between the left of centre Labour Party and the ruling conservative National Party.
Bolger, who continues as caretaker Prime Minister until a new government is formed, said the parties to coalition talks should negotiate in good faith and stop talking in public.
"You won't be getting much more details from now on."
He agreed with New Zealand First leader Winston Peters that negotiations could begin next week.
Earlier Peters had announced his negotiating team and indicated he thought the chances of a deal with Labour or National were about even.

National's team includes Bolger, Foreign Minister Don McKinnon, Finance Minister Bill Birch, Health Minister Jenny Shipley, Justice Minister Doug Graham, Attorney-General Paul East and MPs Roger Sowry, Max Bradford and Georgina Te Heuheu.
